## FS-3 service prerequisite — the native folder choice becomes a saved Files export (2026-10-05)

A current desktop renderer can call `workspace.pickFolder {}` and receive cancellation or
an exported picked root. Electron supplies the attended native choice; fieldd validates
its canonical directory and requires the selection audit before publishing it. Caller
paths are ignored, filesystem roots and unavailable folders are refused, and plain tokens,
plugins, shell-main and remote callers cannot invoke this door. A late choice from a revoked
window, audit failure or failed atomic save creates no export. The audit records the choice;
a subsequent persistence refusal does not turn that selection into a registered root.

Picked folders persist beside places in the existing version-1 roots file, deduplicate by
canonical path, and remain visible as missing when absent or replaced by a symlink.
`WorkspaceClient.pickFolder()` returns the root or null; `attach(root, path?)` keeps its
exact export id and returns an independent recovering port lease even outside the bounded
roots roster. Ticket confinement and the existing read-only direct worker plane still apply.
The public artifact picker keeps its original purpose; Files uses its own principal-gated door.

**Validation:** `pnpm verify` EXIT 0 (`verify-1.log`), started at load 37.54 with
no other verify: fieldd 1,902 passed / 23 opt-in skips; field-app 1,552 passed / 1 skipped;
electron-shell 805 passed / 2 skipped; contracts 817 passed; Rust 302 passed / 9 ignored.
Generation is fresh. The focused checks passed all 380 rows, including 32 Files/service
rows; the shell and renderer also parse the new picker contracts/fixtures. `pnpm smoke`
and `pnpm smoke:godview` each produced their successful product marker and EXIT 0
(`smoke-isolated.log`, `smoke-godview-isolated.log`, start loads 17.90 / 17.52).
Each used a fresh isolated Electron profile and the external offscreen/focus-emulation
harness; no live display or OS input. Godview's offscreen canvas2d fallback and existing
swarm/timing limitations remain outside this Files claim. Receipts are retained at
`/Volumes/SamsungRed/lanes/fs3-service`. No iOS source changed or iOS gate was rerun.

**Scope:** this lands FS-3's service and lease prerequisite. The desk's `FileTree`, decorations,
drag into the composer and pane integration remain DK's consumer work (§5.3 of the FS record).
The native dialog is witnessed through the shell provider fixture, not by OS input on the live
display. The integration test uses real fieldd RPC, a real Files worker, native mille and direct
WebSocket bytes, with fixture native management and dialog responses. No new signed application
was produced in this slice; the earlier packaging receipt remains tied to `c18b7ac2`.

## FS session fix-ups — a live Files session outlives its ticket; each attachment in the ledger; the audit's fixes (2026-10-08; `b05b7172` — nine commits `53c22d2a`→`2d440242` rebased as `…c19de160`, plus the lead's `b05b7172`; lane fsfix over main `bc5553be`, rebased onto `6e706b1d`)

**Why:** James ruled the Files & History Docket on 2026-10-07 (DECISIONS, FS row): **R1 (a)** a ticket's expiry bounds REDEMPTION only, and **R6 (a)** the 10-07 audit's fixes plus per-attach audit rows. Until now the listener revoked a live pair at `expiresAt` and the client re-attached every ~9.5 minutes, so History's file column flashed "Opening the worktree", collapsed its tree, lost scroll and selection, closed any open file/diff/commit, and a file action mid-swap answered "The folder changed; try again".

**What landed:**
- **R1.** The worker's expiry timer runs only until both legs serve; a pair not established by `expiresAt` (unredeemed or half-redeemed) is dropped, both legs; an established session has no timer. The client no longer re-attaches on a timer and keeps its generation. `RENEW_BEFORE_MS` is gone; `TICKET_TTL_MS`'s comment says what it bounds. Every real end still closes both legs: close, a leg closing, root loss, principal revocation, root withdrawal, worker or fieldd restart.
- **Per-attach audit rows (R6).** `workspace.session.establish` / `workspace.session.end` (system actor), target the mint's `{workspace-root, rootId}`, attrs `{clientId, generation}`, reasons `CLOSED · LEG_CLOSED · ROOT_LOST · PRINCIPAL_REVOKED · ROOT_WITHDRAWN · WORKER_STOPPED · WORKER_EXITED`; the mint and its session rows share one `attachId`; the supervisor ends what a dead or stopped generation held; pending rows drain before audit closes. No paths recorded.
- **A place keeps its identity.** An additive roots-file v1 `realPath`, recorded at touch; refresh marks a place missing when its real path changed or is a filesystem root, so a folder swapped for a symlink (even to `/`) is no longer followed. `/tmp` and `/var` places (system links) stay present; a legacy place adopts its real path on its first usable refresh, never a filesystem root.
- **The viewport cap is named:** `WORKSPACE_LIMITS.MAX_VIEWPORT_ROWS = 2_048` in `TREE_SESSION_POLICY` (mille's `maxViewportRows`); an oversized request is clamped and the client told `VIEWPORT_CLAMPED`, never refused.
- The worker's uncalled `git` control-pipe op is retired. `workspace.fileAction` is `idempotent: false` (reveal repeats a side effect; the flag only keys forwarded mutations).
- **Docs at their sources:** wall R24 was right — nothing imports `@vibecook/mille/browser` and mille `baa0de8` exports no `./browser`; dated errata in `CLAUDE.md`, `architecture.html` and `api.html`; the R24 header, the `pnpm-workspace.yaml` pin comment and the `agent-session` `/private` note corrected. The lead added `api.html`'s expiry erratum and `host/git.ts`'s: its header claimed a repository's own config never makes a read run a program, but rosetta's RO-15 lane showed on git 2.50.1 that a `.gitattributes` clean filter still runs on status/diff (git cannot turn filters off). Not an EL7 breach: the worker runs without the daemon's env prefixes.
- **Phone:** a Files no-door refusal is tagged `workspace`/`no_door` (it borrowed the terminal's tag), still shown as "<desktop> is asleep"; a kit test that picked roots list under Browse and open (the pick-folder golden mirrored byte-for-byte).

**Validation** (`/Volumes/SamsungRed/lanes/fsfix/`): `pnpm verify` verbatim on the lane tip `2d440242` was RED twice under load — `verify.log` (start load ~38, rising past 90 with four other lanes and another lead's MV lanes building; field-app `design-system.test.tsx` timeouts) and `verify-2.log` (timeouts in electron-shell artifact-preview-capture and support-bundle, fieldd service-drain and `workspace-git` gitFacts) — each failing test passed alone, and the failures did not repeat across runs. `verify-3.log` on the same tip: **EXIT 0**, full chain incl. `gen:check` (contracts 818 passed). `pnpm smoke` EXIT 0 and `pnpm smoke:godview` EXIT 0, both offscreen with fresh profiles (`smoke.log`, `smoke-godview.log`). iOS kit tests `** TEST SUCCEEDED **` (`ios-tests-1.log`, DerivedData in the lane; incl. `pickedRootsShowUnderBrowseAndOpen`). The landing rebase crossed only `6e706b1d` (docs/DECISIONS.md) and the lead's fix-up is comments and HTML only (biome clean, preflight `EXIT 0`), so the gate was not re-run.

**Known, not fixed:** (1) most user closes record `LEG_CLOSED`, not `CLOSED` — the renderer's sockets close before its `closeTicket` reaches the worker, and the first cause wins; (2) a SIGKILLed fieldd leaves an establish row with no end row, and nothing reconciles at the next boot; (3) places get no worker-side canonical check at mint (picks do) — fieldd's JS realpath and the worker's native one can differ in letter case on APFS; refresh around the mint and the worker's root check cover all but a swap reversed within milliseconds.

## PJ-1a — one normalizer, the grouping engine in fieldd, and a redacted witness (2026-10-08; `f6235540` — five commits `a67b98d3` place facts' wire shape · `91122d68` the normalizer, `familyOf` delegating, the key, the place kind · `134330bd` the engine · `f3348c56` the redacted corpus · `f6235540` the witness; lane pj1a over main `80c000f7`, fast-forward)

**Why:** PJ-D1…D24 RULED 2026-10-07 at every lean (DECISIONS, PJ row); PJ-1 is AR-8e's first slice. Plan of record `draft/project-places/build-pj.md` (decisions L1–L8).

**What landed:**
- **Contracts** `project-places.ts`: `PlaceFacts` (§9's fields plus `git: boolean` and `homeRelative?`, so no home path ships; hits `{placeId, sha, depth}`, SHAs 40 or 64 hex at the wire), tolerant lists (`PlaceFactsList` drops only an unreadable place, so one bad place never costs a mesh row of session history); `IndexCatalogProject.places?` (L1 — places ride the catalog's project rows, no new table); `GROUPING_VERSION = 1`, `PROJECT_GROUPING {SAMPLE_DEPTHS, RECENT_DEPTH 16, INK_DEALS 997}`. New fixtures only; `index-projects.mesh.json` and its three iOS mirrors untouched.
- **One normalizer** (`fieldd/src/projects/normalize.ts`) — DS-D9's `familyOf` now delegates to it (L4, a lockstep event): a remote's path folds case on every host, a `www.` prefix drops, percent-escapes decode; every other DS-D9 row unchanged; local paths and host-only remotes still have no family. The prototype's userinfo leak is fixed (the host follows the LAST `@`, so a password containing `@` never reaches a key; `file:` userinfo dropped), alias maps read only their own keys.
- **The key (L5):** `p1:` + base32 of the first 128 bits of SHA-256 over `vibefield/project-key/v1\0` + identity — UNKEYED, a recorded deviation from the record's "keyed SHA-256" until a secret shared across one user's desktops exists; a record-less ink from the same digest mod 997.
- **The engine** (`fieldd/src/projects/grouping.ts`), a pure strict-TS port of the prototype's `evidence` strategy plus intents (empty intents = G2): evidence groups, Home and Temporary buckets, suggestions with `via` (the root, remote, folder or name in common) instead of English, records bound by anchor. It sorts its own input, so a replica's arrival order cannot change a name, a representative pair or an edge; two spellings of one folder answer to both ids. No clock input.
- **The place kind** (`place-kind.ts`) is ONE rule the files worker will call (build-pj M1).

**The witness** (`fieldd/test/project-grouping-witness.test.ts` over `test/fixtures/projects/places-corpus.json`): the Mac's 161 places → **132 rows** (Home 2, Temporary 26; 2 multi-place; suggestions related-history 1, same-name 2); three desktops → **143 rows** (9 multi-place, 8 across desktops); with the one link (§4.4's G3) → 142; **0 trap pairs** over C8a, C8b, C10, C11, C13, C15, C19 (0 false merges, 0 false splits); clear groups 11/11 exact (46 true pairs, 0 wrong, 0 missed); the invariants hold (keys unique and opaque; a deleted clone keeps key and ink; a record binds and keeps its ink; an unnamed later record adds no name; the oldest named record names the group). The 8 `?`-labelled judgments stay unscored, awaiting J1–J11 on the docket. Off the repo, the builder ran the same `witnessOf` on the UNREDACTED corpus and on three fresh redactions — deep-equal every time — and the prototype's own `group()` gives the port's groupings exactly; a mutation (a C8a hit forced to depth 1) gives a false merge, so the trap score can fail.

**Redaction (L8):** `scripts/redact-places-corpus.mjs` replaces every owner, repository, folder, branch and SHA with a random token of random length (6–11) per run, stores no mapping, drops session titles and refuses to write unless every output part is a minted token or a kept word with no 40-hex and no `/Users/`. Scanned by the builder (369 distinct real segments, owners, repos, branches, heads, SHAs, labels — none present) and independently by the lead (no added line carries a corpus name). The repo is public.

**Validation** (`/Volumes/SamsungRed/lanes/pj1a/`): `pnpm verify` EXIT 0 (contracts project-places 5; fieldd project-grouping 16, project-normalize 40, project-family 51, project-grouping-witness 9), `pnpm smoke` EXIT 0, `pnpm smoke:godview` EXIT 0 (offscreen, fresh profiles), no reruns.

**Next:** lane pj1b (the hardened runner, the worker's place facts, the scanner and the catalog enrichment) rebases onto this and runs the engine over local ∪ replica facts. Doors are PJ-3.

## PJ-1b — place facts: one hardened git runner, the worker's `placeFacts`, the scanner, and the projects held in fieldd (2026-10-08; `f6d57ced` — twelve commits `c9d9c66f`→`f6d57ced`; lane pj1b over main `02d47d18`, fast-forward). **PJ-1 is complete.**

**What landed:**
- **One hardened git runner** in the files worker for every caller (the git port, `gitFacts`, place facts): an environment ALLOWLIST (PATH, HOME, USER, LANG, `LC_*`, TMPDIR, a few Windows variables — no `GIT_*`), `core.hooksPath=/dev/null`, `protocol.allow=never` plus every transport refused by name (a repository's own config can re-allow one past `protocol.allow=never`), `core.fsmonitor=false`, `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1`, `log.showSignature=false`, a per-call timeout and a worker-wide cap of 6 (`WORKSPACE_GIT.CONCURRENCY`). `safe.directory` is never set: a refused repository is the fact `gitRefused: "dubious-ownership"`. Place facts never run `git status` (a `.gitattributes` clean filter would run).
- **`placeFacts`** (a worker op): real path, exists, mounted, caseless (probed per volume), kind (ONE rule, `placeKindOf`: a task root holds what is below it; case folds only on a caseless volume; `/` and drive roots are `home`), `homeRelative`; head, branch, the guarded first-parent root, samples at `PROJECT_GROUPING.SAMPLE_DEPTHS`, remotes and the push remote, ssh aliases via `ssh -G` for a guarded host pattern only, `worktreeOf` and sibling worktrees (from a working tree's top only); hits in one `cat-file --batch-check` and one `rev-list --stdin`. Cached by key with a per-question budget.
- **The scanner** reads every root of each local rosetta project plus their worktrees on boot, on a change of project roots, on peer changes and every 5 minutes; each place's facts ride its catalog project row (`IndexCatalogProject.places`, no new table); `observedAt` moves only when facts change; a missing folder keeps its last-known git facts; `acted` comes from the files service's roots by longest prefix. The mesh replica reads `places` tolerantly (a non-list reads as none, so a newer peer cannot drop its projects from an older desktop's History). `index.projects` answers WITHOUT `places` until PJ-3 decides what crosses to a window or the phone. **`taskRoots`** joins the agent catalog (PJ-D21; the generated fixture and its five kit mirrors).
- **`ProjectGroups`** (`fieldd/src/projects/project-groups.ts`) runs the engine over this desktop's places ∪ every peer's (`IndexMesh.peerRows`); sessions join a place by longest cwd prefix; same-device hits join a remote-less repository's worktrees (`worktreeOf` is not a join rule); the result is held for PJ-3 (no door), an unchanged input computes nothing, one log line per change of the grouping (counts only).

**Witnesses:** the corpus's three desktops publish their places on rows and replicate through the real rows protocol into IndexMesh — grouping on the Mac gives **143 rows, 8 across desktops**, with the partition and every key equal to the engine run directly, and a replica that loses its places fails the test. A real-git test: a remote-less checkout, its worktree and a remote-less clone become ONE `local` project joined only by history. Mutation probes turned the hardening, hits and replica tests red. A live read-only run over six real repositories: 123 places, 4 projects, an unchanged pass 3.3 s.

**Validation** (`/Volumes/SamsungRed/lanes/pj1b/`): `pnpm verify` verbatim on `f6d57ced` — **`verify25.log` EXIT 0** (started at 1-minute load 20.9, the full chain through `gen:check`; fieldd 2 050 passed, field-app 1 553, contracts 829, `cargo test` ok); `pnpm smoke` and `pnpm smoke:godview` EXIT 0 offscreen (run 6, same tip). Earlier verify runs on this tip were RED twice, both proven not this lane's: run 5 on the `artifact-service` clock flake (below), run 6 on load timeouts — field-app `design-system.test.tsx` ×2 (this lane changes no field-app or design-kit file) and fieldd's AC-3 census test, measured alone 3× on main and 3× on the tip at ~3.6 s each against a 5 s budget (the lead re-ran the tip side independently: 3 558–3 671 ms). The workspace-engine "at the cap" test: 5 alternating rounds alone, base vs tip, 9/9 both sides, the tip never slower.

**Known, not fixed:** `packages/electron-shell/…/artifact-service.test.ts:1107` asserts a slice's JSON does not match `/…|3000/` while that JSON holds `Date.now()` stamps — it fails whenever a stamp contains "3000" (needs a fixed clock or a narrower pattern). The AC-3 census, design-system and workspace-engine tests run near their timeouts and go red on a loaded host on main as well. A peer's `acted` reads false (not on the wire).

## PJ-3 — the `project.*` doors: projects for a window and the phone, keys that move, paths by P1 (2026-10-08; `e103d48b` — six commits `fb80e9da` contracts · `3b40d313` the key memory · `59fcee8f` the doors · `2e188bdc` the phone's witness · `0fc4a02e` an erratum at `index.projects`' source · `e103d48b` J11's per-desktop Home; lane pj3 over main `7e55ea57`, rebased over docs-only commits)

**Why:** PJ-D15 (a) — `project.*` doors with `asOf`/`movedTo`/`regrouped`, a `project.read` scope never plugin-eligible; James's 2026-10-08 rulings P1 (a) (the Files service's path rule: the phone never sends a path, answers to the user's own devices may carry one, a guest never) and P2 (a) (only desktop windows write acts); J11 (Home is a project, one per desktop). Plan `draft/project-places/build-pj23.md`.

**What landed:**
- **Contracts** (`contracts/src/project-doors.ts`, TS only): `PlaceRef {device, placeId}`; `ProjectSummary` v2 — key, provisional, name/`nameFrom` (incl. `home`), alsoCalled, ink, kind, `bucket "temp" | null` (Home is a project: `kind: "home"`, one device), devices, places `{ref, name, path? (P1), class, branch?, worktreeOf?, exists, mounted, sessions, lastAt?}`, sessions, anchors, `asOf {device: ISO time last heard}`, `groupingVersion`; the five doors' params and results; typed refusals.
- **The doors** (`federate` reads served from `ProjectGroups.current()`; every handler refuses a peer daemon, a guest, a plugin and an MCP agent): `project.list` (keyset on lastAt + the smallest `place:` anchor, which no key move changes; `q` matches names only), `project.get` (follows a moved key and answers `movedTo`; suggestions and edges), `project.sessions` (one row per session, joined to its place by longest cwd prefix), `project.subscribe` (rows pings with `regrouped [{from, to}]`; a cursor resumes while the move log covers it, else a snapshot reset), `project.intent` (`settings.manage`, `sync`, not idempotent — each act carries its time; an act on a moved key is refused `key-moved`; answers UNAVAILABLE `records-unbuilt` until PJ-2's writer is wired).
- **Key memory** (`fieldd/src/projects/key-journal.ts`): the last key each place was seen under; old → new moves inferred at each regroup (a scattered key follows most of its places, a tie the smaller key); bounded, persisted atomically (`LAYOUT.PROJECT_KEYS_FILE`), opaque ids only; survives a restart.
- **What a tailnet caller sees:** paths only for a self principal (P1) and none when `self` is absent; only `place:` anchors (root/remote anchors would spell what `via` does); no `via`, no aliases. A request naming a path anywhere — in a PlaceRef, as `cwd`, as a `remote:local:` anchor, on the pings — is refused `PRECONDITION_FAILED {reason: path-in-request, field}`.
- **`project.read`** in `SCOPES` and the phone's preset (so the peer preset by derivation — every handler refuses the peer), the window's token, never in `PLUGIN_CAPABILITY_ELIGIBILITY`; `PROJECT_DOORS` numbers; `LAYOUT.PROJECTS_DIR` with registries.rs and layout.json regenerated.

**The witness** (`fieldd/test/project-doors-phone.test.ts`, 8 rows, one real daemon dialled through the sidecar door): the phone lists its desktop's projects with paths (self); its sessions join their places; a guest is refused every read; four path-naming asks are refused with the field named; a fork moves the app's key and `project.get`/`project.sessions` on the old key answer `movedTo`, the subscription hears `regrouped`, the key file reads the move back; the peer is refused all reads and the act; the phone's act is FORBIDDEN_SCOPE and the window's UNAVAILABLE `records-unbuilt`; a plugin never holds `project.read`. Red proofs: admitting `peer-fieldd` and always answering paths each turn a row red.

**Validation** (`/Volumes/SamsungRed/lanes/pj3/`): on `929c2b3b` (rebased to `e103d48b` over `docs/DECISIONS.md` only) `pnpm verify` EXIT 0 (fieldd 2 088 passed, field-app 1 553), `pnpm smoke` and `pnpm smoke:godview` EXIT 0 offscreen. Earlier runs on `0fc4a02e` were red twice on load timeouts (agent-session AR-S4c and MF-1f/g at load 147; design-system hooks), each re-run alone green; run 3 there was green too.

**Next:** PJ-2 (records) rebases onto this and wires `project.intent` to its writer.

## PJ-2 — project records in the library, the person's acts honoured, and `project.intent` live (2026-10-08; `6c4e8621` — eleven commits `dad6ec87`→`6c4e8621`; lane pj2 over main `bab6956a`, fast-forward)

**Why:** PJ-D19 (a) records made only by acts; PJ-D5/P3 (a) a record freezes the project's provisional ink; P2 (a) desktop windows write acts; J1–J11 (James, 2026-10-08), with J11 amending PJ-D3: a desktop's Home is a project, one per desktop. Plan `draft/project-places/build-pj23.md` (D1–D7).

**What landed:**
- **placeIds re-keyed to a stable id (§0).** The scanner hashed the roster id, which moves at link (`local-<uuid>` → the mesh ULID), at relink (truffle mints a new ULID after native `retire`) and at the boot of a linked desktop before its mesh is up — a test showed one folder publish three placeIds. They now hash the persisted local id (`localDeviceIdAt`, `DeviceService.localDeviceId()`), which no link moves; every placeId changed once at this upgrade, before any record existed. Dated errata at the three sources that said "moves at most once".
- **Records in DS-5's library** (`projects/records-doc.ts`), root maps of their own: grow-only `projects.created/anchors/acted/links/splits/dismissals`, last-writer-wins `projects.names/inks/recipes/pinned/hidden`; one act is one commit; an older desktop carries the maps untouched.
- **`ProjectRecords`:** a project's first act creates its record and freezes its provisional ink (P3); rename, pin, hide, link (a place joins this project), split, dismiss, and `actedIn(cwd)` for runs the person started (a boot re-attach is not an act); `setRecipe` for PJ-6; a relink carries local-account records into the linked account only, and a failed carry never fails the boot.
- **The engine honours acts** (`GROUPING_VERSION` 2): a split is bound to a record and the later act wins for a pair; a dismissal binds to the pair of records; under an unnamed oldest record the oldest named record names the group. **J11:** each desktop's home folder, `/` and drive roots form that desktop's own Home project (`kind`/`nameFrom` `home`, joined to nothing; link/split/dismiss refused `home`); Temporary is the only bucket.
- **`project.intent` is live:** the door writes through `ProjectRecords` (rename/pin/hide pass through; `link {place}` and `split {place}` by PlaceRef; `dismiss {with}`); new typed refusals `not-a-project`, `home`, `only-place`, `same-project`, and UNAVAILABLE `records-remounting` (retryable) while a relink swaps the library; the phone stays FORBIDDEN_SCOPE (P2). A first record's `p1:` → `r:` is journalled by PJ-3's key memory, so the old key answers `movedTo`.

**Witnesses:** two desktops on the real doc mesh, each with a real `ProjectDoors` — a window's rename on A through its door reads on B with `nameFrom: "you"` and the same ink, B's `project.get` on the OLD key answers `movedTo`, and an act on the old key is refused `key-moved`; a split gives each record back its side; renames made while partitioned converge; two simultaneous first acts freeze the same ink and agree on one key. James's judgments J1–J11 are scored truth on the redacted corpus: 47 true pairs, 0 wrong joins, 0 misses, 11/11 exact groups, 0 trap pairs; **Mac 132 rows, three desktops 145** (PJ-1's 143 counted one Home bucket), G3 144; redacted = unredacted. The judgments file names folders, so it lives only in `draft/project-places/test/` (dev-local); the redaction script refuses to run without it.

**Validation** (`/Volumes/SamsungRed/lanes/pj2/`): `pnpm verify` verbatim on `6c4e8621` — `lead-verify-2.log` **EXIT 0** (the lead's run, started at 1-minute load 6.7). Both smokes EXIT 0 twice on its parent `8199070a` (the last commit adds 11 test lines). The builder's own gate on `6c4e8621` then passed whole: `attempt1-verify.log`, `attempt1-smoke.log`, `attempt1-smoke-godview.log`, each EXIT 0. ## MV — Godview's monitor views are SDK modules over one backend (2026-10-08; `7a0893d8` — the merge of `mv/land` `db355ea7` onto main `1adde1a6`, gated in the lane land-vf; puppeteer main `6392865` → `594d222`; then ghosttea `8a0930e` → `10d0b17` as its own EL8 commit `4387a973`)

**Why:** James's monitor-view rulings of 2026-10-03 are the frame:
- views are pure presentation;
- ONE backend per desktop, beside the runtime, and only its model syncs;
- one view is mounted at a time, and a view never modifies anything outside itself;
- "godview should stay runtime only";
- only rosetta ingests transcripts.

Within it sit the contract's 21 marks (MV-D1…D22, D16 marks only), built as `draft/monitor-view-sdk/build-mv.md` (M1–M202). James ruled the last wave's nine asks on 2026-10-07 ("good, go with your lean, plan and go", M177), and landed it with "land it" (2026-10-08 19:34 UTC).

**What landed:**
- **The SDK and the one backend.**
  - `@vibecook/puppeteer-view-sdk`: the contract, `/react`, `/host`, `/testing` and `/toolkit`.
  - `@vibecook/puppeteer-monitor` runs beside the runtime, one per desktop: in fieldd, and in Electron main in puppeteer's Godview.
  - Windows and the phone hold replicas of its model (MV-D22, D18).
- **Godview's five views are SDK modules:** list, rain, swarm, timeline and spend.
  - Spend is MV-7: the runtime-only watchlist, ported as built (M177 ruling 2). SV-D15…D19 are ruled later.

- **Chrome boundaries** (M49) wrap every piece of Godview's chrome in both hosts.

- **Also:**
  - AR-7b's test asserts what AR-7b guards (ruling 9).
  - fieldd's docs-holders stop is bounded at 2 s (`DOC_HOLDERS_STOP_MS`).
  - The Godview smoke runner spawns Electron itself, with no shell.
  - The old `.vibefield/dev/data/users/1/agents/history/` (7 files, 1,870 bytes) is removed (ruling 6).

## AR-8 History gaps — recorded images draw, paths read `~/…`, delegated threads under their parent (2026-10-08; `3ec58bf7` — three commits `cbe07166` attachments · `2d320641` the home door · `3ec58bf7` threads; lane hist over main `8ae3da5c`, fast-forward)

**Why:** James's "go" on finishing History (2026-10-08). AR-8c's owed list named attachments, the home door and delegated threads. Plan `draft/history-finish/build-hf.md` (§2 the defects, §3 L1, L2 and L4).

**Defects this fixes (found by the read-only survey):**
- **D1.** Every recorded image in History read "Image data was not recorded". The room asks `imageAssetUrl` only when `attachmentAssetUrl` is non-null, and ours answered null.
- **D2.** A search hit inside a subagent's thread was dropped silently. fieldd kept children out of the room's meta, and the room drops a hit whose session it cannot see.

**What landed:**
- **Attachments.** `attachmentAssetUrl` answers the asset's stable rosettad path (`/api/assets/<digest>.webp`) when the ref names rosettad's own route, and null otherwise. Recorded images now draw from grant-read bytes as bounded object URLs. Non-image attachments still say "Attachment preview unavailable", as in rosetta's own app.
- **The home door (L2).** History's host port answers `homeDir` from the window's bootstrap home (`WindowConnection.terminal.home`, the same OS user rosettad indexes), through a plain getter. A browser or catalog harness answers null.
- **Delegated threads (L1).**
  - Storage: children of a root session live in a local-only, never-replicated `threads` table in IndexCatalog. A thread is held while its root is listed and leaves with it. A child that arrives before its root waits for the next snapshot.
  - The door: `index.threads {cursor?, limit? 1..500}` is window-only (`local-token`, `shell-main`; FORBIDDEN_SCOPE to plugins, MCP agents, the phone and guests), scope `index.search`, locality `local`, keyset-paged by root then id.
  - Row shape: `parentSessionId`, `rootSessionId`, an open `role`, and `delegation` as a camelCase passthrough projection that the renderer maps back to rosetta's `SessionDelegation`.
  - Pings: `INDEX_CATALOG_TABLES` names `threads`. A new `INDEX_REPLICATED_TABLES` (projects, sessions) types `index.catalog.subscribe` and the mesh replica, so `table: "threads"` is refused. Local pings now name their table, and the renderer re-reads only the table that moved.
  - Unchanged: the `sessions` table, `sessionCount`, `index.sessions`, `project.*`, the mesh and the phone stay roots-only.
- **Errata at source:** `doors.ts`'s claims that fieldd sends only home-abbreviated paths, and that there is no worktree guest until AR-8d; `system.html`'s "no worktree port", corrected with the home door and the attachment address.

**Witnesses** (real rosettad at `856bd80`, synthesized homes per L4; logs in `/Volumes/SamsungRed/lanes/hist/logs/`):
- **D1, render:** the shipping `HistoryRoomView` draws both demo images as `blob:` URLs with no "not recorded" words. Red with `() => null` restored.
- **D1, real:** a 1×1 PNG in a Claude prompt becomes an optimized WebP with four renditions. The tile and full renditions arrive as RIFF/WEBP bytes under the grant, a bare fetch gets 401, and fieldd is asked only `index.openTicket`. Red without the fix.
- **L2:** `~/Projects/vibe-field` shows for a root under home, and `/opt/build/tools` stays in full. Red with `homeDir: null`.
- **L1/D2, fieldd:** catalog, door and mesh rows.
  - Red-proof: with the table split reverted, the 4 thread rows go red while the 16 root rows stay green.
- **L1/D2, real history witness:** a synthesized `subagents/agent-<id>.jsonl` under its parent reaches meta with role `subagent` and the Agent tool's id. It opens on its own ticket with no fieldd frame carrying it, and a hit inside it resolves to its root. The EL2 door-call checks admit `index.threads`.
  - Red-proof: the witness goes red with the split reverted, and the search row goes red with the hit mapping reverted.

**Validation:** the lane's `gate.sh` on `3ec58bf7`, the landed tree (main had not moved), Nx cache skipped. `verify.log` **EXIT 0** (typecheck and test for 25 projects; field-app 1,587, fieldd 2,157 passed with 6 skipped, contracts 884). `smoke.log` EXIT 0, `smoke-godview.log` EXIT 0. The first gate's verify was red only on load timeouts at 1-minute load 254, in files outside the diff (fieldd AR-S4c sign-in, `design-system.test.tsx`, `godview-model-stream.test.ts`); each was green on a rerun.

**Found on the way:**
- James's `../puppeteer` install predates view-sdk, so field-app's `tsc` fails with TS2307 in any tree linking it. Lanes now use their own installed worktree at the lock's pin.
- The lanes' offscreen preload broke `smoke:godview` after MV's `labProfileProof`; it now leaves a runner's `--user-data-dir` alone (found by lane pkg).
- rosetta's Claude reader drops a record whose `usage` has fewer fields than the ground truth, counting it as a hard error.

**Upstream asks (petitions):**
- `tildePath` needs a segment boundary: home `/Users/me` turns `/Users/meg/notes` into `~g/notes`.
- The room's fixtures carry no delegated thread.
- A narrower `usage` should be drift, not a lost record.
- Export the room's search grouping for a DOM-free host test.

## AR-8 packaged History — rosettad and the agent shim ship in the app; the packaged origin witnessed end to end (2026-10-08; `4dd952c5` — five commits `1cb558cf`→`4dd952c5`; lane pkg over main `8ae3da5c`, rebased by the lead onto `4531284f`, fast-forward)

**Why:** James's "go" on finishing History (2026-10-08). Plan `draft/history-finish/build-hf.md` L3: packaged rosettad is optional, like the screenshot helper. LANDED §FS packaging closeout's "Still owed" named packaged rosettad and `agent-shim.cjs` beside fieldd.

**What landed:**
- **Staged and resolved.**
  - `stage-package.mjs` stages `bin/rosettad` from the lock's own build (`rosettadBinary()`), optional unless `--require-complete`. It warns, without refusing, when a Rust source is newer than the binary. It also stages `bin/agent-shim.cjs` beside the fieldd SEA.
  - `electron-builder.yml` lists `Contents/Resources/bin/rosettad` under `mac.binaries`.
  - `resources.ts` gains `rosettadPath` (packaged `Resources/bin/rosettad[.exe]`, dev null). It checks the arch only when the binary is present (`rosettad-arch-mismatch`).
  - `main/fieldd.ts` sets `FIELDD_ROSETTAD_BIN` from the environment, otherwise from the packaged path when it exists.
- **Words.** `rosettadUnconfigured(packaged)` changes what a SEA fieldd says. It is now "this copy of VibeField was built without agent history — install a build that includes it to read your agents' sessions here". A developer build keeps the variable's name.
- **`package:verify:history`** (`verify-history-package.mjs`; the codesign check moved to a shared `release-signature.mjs`, also used by `verify-files-package.mjs`; run by `run-macos-release.mjs` after signing):
  - It runs fieldd's new `packaged-history.test.ts`, which execs the real SEA behind the mock floor: with no rosettad (the packaged words), and with the packaged rosettad (ready, protocol 26).
  - It runs `index-open-ticket` and `history-witness` against the packaged rosettad, failing on any skipped row.
- **The origin.**
  - `history-witness`'s transport sends `Origin: vibefield-app://shell`. It asserts `access-control-allow-origin` on every read, a 2xx preflight for the grant's header, and a 101 upgrade, and that a foreign origin gets neither.
  - `smoke:godview`'s History rung now seeds one Claude transcript in the person's HOME, enrolls it, opens the session from the real page and waits for its words. It forces a preflighted grant read, with Chromium's Network domain recording the traffic (`testing/loopback-network.ts`).

**Signed** (`/Volumes/SamsungRed/lanes/pkg/`, "package signé", `--dir`, notarize off, nothing installed or opened):
- rosettad is signed Developer ID (team 9F79X9D26S), with a secure timestamp and the hardened runtime.
- The signed SEA started the signed rosettad under the hardened runtime: `verify-history-signed.log` EXIT 0, 23 rows.
- Deep verify, the fuses (9) and the Files verifier (34/34) are all EXIT 0.
- `--require-signed` refuses an unsigned rosettad, as it should.

**Chromium's local-network access (Electron 43.1.1 / Chromium 150):** it did not engage. No `access-control-request-*` or private/local-network headers were sent, no load was blocked and no permission was denied. In the smoke, the WebSocket GET answered 101, the fetch GET 200 and the OPTIONS preflight 200, each carrying the app origin and its allow-origin.

**Validation:** the lead's gate on `4dd952c5`, the landed tree: `verify.log` **EXIT 0** (no Nx cache), `smoke.log` EXIT 0, `smoke-godview.log` EXIT 0. The rebase resolved `history-witness.test.ts` against lane hist's synthesized-home rows, keeping both: hist's `loggedDoor` with pkg's app-origin transport. The packaged receipts are from the pre-rebase build (rosetta `856bd80`, mille `baa0de8`).

**Debts found (ROADMAP's open debts):**
- Every shipped Rust daemon inherits `allow-jit`, rosettad included. electron-builder 26 has no per-file entitlements, so a custom sign step is needed.
- `package-census --assert --strict` is red on MV's renderer chunks (lab-bridge, lab-switches, theme; client chunk count 2). The baseline needs an `--update`.
- A smoke that dies early leaves rosettad orphaned (ppid 1).
- Shipped Rust binaries embed `~/.cargo/registry` paths carrying the build user's name; `--remap-path-prefix` would fix it.
- The staged shim is not yet a launcher under a SEA fieldd (AR-7j).
- A signed build with no rosettad or screenshot helper fails codesign while release stages with `--require-complete`.
- Petition: the room titles the unconfigured state "rosettad is not answering", which names a daemon to a person.

**What landed — the Peek (P1):**

  - §8: a new entry, "Search — the Peek". §8 History is rewritten: the band holds the button, ⌘G/⇧⌘G retire (K3), and the empty transcript says "Pick a session, or search with ⌘F." (K2).

- **The Peek** (`frame/peek*`) is one 900×560 popup over the scrim. It has Live now and Everything (History opens on Everything; Live now says live sessions are searched in Godview until P2, K9), three dropdowns (project, prompts and replies, agent), the list (rows grouped by root; a neutral match, K1), the past peek (the session's matched lines, K8), and a foot with "Open at the line ↵".
  - ⌘F (Ctrl+F off a Mac) is a product chord while History is the view (K4); Settings → Keyboard says it is kept from a pane.
  - Keys: ↑↓, ↵, Esc. One surface at a time. The field is inert under the Peek and focus returns on close.
  - Narrow windows clamp to 24 px clear at the sides and 96 at the top and foot, folding below a 680 popup (K6).
  - Everything is local until DS-7 (K5).
- **Open at the line.** A past row calls the room's `openAt({sessionId, timelineId})` through a module-store door that HistoryView consumes. A hit inside a delegated thread rides its root's row and opens there through `index.threads` (D2 carried from the retired interim test).
- **`index.search` hits** carry their root's `cwd`, `projectId` and agent, additively, with fixtures. A quoted phrase matches whole on the real rosettad (witnessed), so the empty sentence may say so.
- **The interim retires:** `history/search.ts` and its test, the room's `search` prop, the `history-search` surface and ⌘G/⇧⌘G. The catalog's interim plate gives way to two Peek plates over the shipping view.
- **The recede under a cover (M7).** GV-D8's recede and DK-15 (§6: no transform reaches the desk's own box under a cover) meet in one full-window `.field-recede` box holding the still and the chrome. That box recedes to 0.98 and `.field-scene` never does. At rest the box makes no stacking context and takes no pointer (`:where(.field-recede) > * { pointer-events: auto }`).

**What landed — Jump to (P3):**
- **Liveness.** One plain `agent.list`, no subscription (PF6: a closed Godview asks nothing), joined on the room's native id. A session is live when its run is not stamped ended and its terminal is on this desktop's floor. It is asked again on a new choice, when History shows again, and at every press. The create keeps its last word while an answer is on the way, so nothing flickers.
- **The line's create.** "Jump to this session" under the `jump` glyph while the session runs here, Resume otherwise. The palette follows the same door.
  - Pressed: Godview opens and `LineViewDoor.reveal(sessionId)` brings forward the pane showing that floor session, else mounts it in the active pane. This is Godview's one new verb; puppeteer and the view modules are untouched.
  - Notes: "Jumped to its pane" / "Could not jump — …".
- **Resume refuses a running session** with "This session is running — Jump to it", and the create flips. Before P3, fieldd already refused a second run of a live conversation (PRECONDITION_FAILED `terminal-alive`, AR-4b's one-run law), so nothing ever ran twice. What was missing was the act and the words, and the survey's "defect lead" was that. fieldd's `terminal-alive` refusal gets the same words.

## TL — Godview's timeline reads the past from the record: rosetta's turns through fieldd's doors and the monitor's port, lent to the view as `history` (2026-10-10; main `bda60ddd`, sha for sha — twenty-one commits: nineteen as first gated, `fc8beb87`→`0f886cf6`, the pins `facd8139` and `ba73674f`, then `7615f6e6` · `915a0834` · `a87d73c5` · `70cef98c`; and the window's two fixes the perf reading found, `c070b1fc` · `bda60ddd`; lane tl cherry-picked onto PJ-4 phase B by lane land2, chain `land/wave2` over main `61fd2a3b`; rosetta `2a91bf0`, puppeteer `c20a07d`)

**Why:** James ruled docket v9 on 2026-10-09 (23:03–23:17), every lean.
- T0 (a), split. The mark's words, where "I" is the History lead: "I build the read (rosetta's route, fieldd's door, the monitor's port); the MV lead draws it in the view."
- T1 (a): worked and quiet, ended and live lanes, from rosetta's turns. Blocked and unseen are never guessed, and a silence over 15 min stays "not recorded".
- T2 (a): the view's 24 hours.
- T3 (a): the same wake.
- T4 (a): a new rosetta route.
- T5 (a): a first version before the route, with ended runs as one band each.
- T6 (a): the map of the day from the same turns.
- The lead's B-D4 (shaped per desktop, built for this one first), B-D5 (the phone later) and B-D6 (backend-owned).
- TIMELINE SHAPES v2, agreed with the MV lead (M10), and the MV lead's ruling on filters (M13).

It is TL-D8's successor under the laws of 2026-10-03: Godview records nothing, only rosetta reads transcripts, and a view draws only what it is lent. James said "Merge" for the three repos on 2026-10-10 (M20). The plan is `draft/history-finish/build-hf.md` §3c–§3d and §5 (M10–M13, M19–M21), with briefs `briefs/tl.md` and `briefs/land2.md`. The contract is `surveys/timeline-shapes-v1.md` with `timeline-shapes-v2-mv-answer.md`; the MV lead's gate asks are `surveys/mv-lead-combined-gate-2026-10-10.md`.

**What landed:**
- **rosetta: `GET /api/activity`** (`db6dd7e` on `vf/activity-route`, carried as `2a91bf0`). Every top-level session's turn spans in a time window, from rosettad's own tables.
  - `TurnSpan {group_id, kind, first_at, last_at, gaps}`. A gap is a stretch between activity instants longer than `gap_ms` (15 min by default).
  - The window is at most seven days. `limit` truncates and says so. A Pending session's turns are withheld.
  - Bearer-only. PROTOCOL_VERSION 26 → 27. No schema change, and nothing stored.
- **puppeteer: the history capability and the port** (`vf/monitor-history-port`, four commits `53e6828`→`a4f088e`).
  - view-sdk: `MonitorCapabilities.history` is `MonitorHistory` (it was `never`), a minor (MV-D10). The manifest is the ask (`viewWantsHistory`). `keepPast` and `lendHistory` are the host's helpers; `fixtureHistory` is for tests and labs.
  - monitor: `CreateMonitorBackendOptions.history?: MonitorHistoryPort` and `MonitorBackend.readPast(window)`, asked on demand and held nowhere.
  - The derivation (`past.ts`): worked inside a turn, quiet between turns, unrecorded across a silence over 15 min, and `bounds` for the floor.
  - Only this runtime's runs are lanes. A `past:` id is no command. An ended lane's colour is read, never dealt.
- **Contracts: two doors.**
  - `index.activity {sinceMs, untilMs, sessions?, silenceMs?, device?}` → `IndexActivityResult {fidelity: "turns" | "bounds", partial, detail?, clipped?, sessions}`. Scope `index.search`, `federate`.
  - `agent.recordedLanes {sinceMs, untilMs, device?}` → `AgentRecordedLanesResult`, the SDK's `MonitorPastSnapshot` field for field. Span kinds are worked, quiet, unrecorded and bounds; states are complete, partial and unavailable. It is not the removed `agent.history`.
  - `INDEX_ACTIVITY` in the registries: the day, T1's 15-minute cut, the session ceiling.
  - Readers for rosetta's wire (`IndexActivityResponse`, protocol 27). Its golden is rosetta's own, transcribed verbatim.
- **fieldd.**
  - `index-activity.ts`: the route is preferred, one GET of `/api/activity` per day-window, parsed and never cast. A route that cannot answer gives way to the catalog's session bounds and says `partial`. It never pages `index.timeline`.
  - `monitorHistoryPort(reader, catalog, runs)`: the record's sessions beside the runs THIS runtime ran (`AgentRuntimeService.recordedRuns()`, read off the verified session records). A session rosetta holds that this runtime never ran is no lane.
  - No rosettad configured means no port: `agent.recordedLanes` refuses NOT_FOUND `{service: "agent.monitor", state: "no-record"}`. A rosettad configured but not up answers `unavailable` at once, in a person's words.
  - Reading the past writes no project identity.
  - `agent-monitor.ts`'s header said "never a ledger on disk and never a history door (MV-D22; TL-D8 stands)". It is amended at its source, dated 2026-10-09, with the ruling.
- **The window** (`godview/monitor/monitor-history.ts`, `useMonitorHistory`).
  - It reads only while a mounted view's manifest declares `history`, over the fixed day [now − 24 h, now]. Nothing is read while Godview is closed (PF6).
  - `keepPast` keeps the same snapshot when only `readAt` moved. `MonitorHistory` is built once per snapshot, theme or filter, never per publish.
  - A run leaving the model reads again after 1 s. A seam moving or a row arriving waits 30 s.
  - One re-read is pending at a time, held apart from the watch (`bda60ddd`). A leaving takes a pending read with it; a seam or an arrival is served by the one already wanted. A later publish neither drops it nor puts it off.
  - The rows are watched only while a read could follow (`c070b1fc`): walked once per publish, and not at all for a view that does not ask or a door that said `no-record`. The rows a watch begins with are its baseline.
  - A failed re-read after a good one keeps the last past, marked `partial`. A door that says `no-record` lends nothing and is not asked again.
  - M13: a chosen desktop narrows the ended lanes before they are lent (`narrowPast`); the profile tab recedes them.
- **The marker** (`7615f6e6`): `GODVIEW_MONITOR` gains `history: "absent" | "complete" | "partial" | "unavailable"` and `endedLanes`, read off the lent object and never a view's DOM (MV-5).
- **The view half** (puppeteer `vf/timeline-past-view`, nine commits `74de92d`→`c20a07d`, the MV lead's): the timeline draws a row's recorded past before its current state, and the runs that ended. The MV lead's own account is "The view half" below, placed as written.
- **EL8.**
  - In-lane pins: `fc8beb87` (puppeteer `594d222` → `dcbc359`) and `e5ff2120` (→ `a4f088e`).
  - The landing's pins: `facd8139` (rosetta `3449648` → `2a91bf0`, one sha holding the room's host slots and the activity route) and `ba73674f` (puppeteer `a4f088e` → `c20a07d`).
  - Lane tl's own rosetta pin `43cb4f5f` was dropped from the chain: its one lock line conflicts with PJ-4's. `facd8139` carries its record.
  - Protocol 26 → 27 is lockstep: a rosettad from before the pin reads `incompatible`.
  - As landed: rosetta main `2a91bf0` (only the ref moved; James's checkout stayed on his own branch) and puppeteer main `c20a07d`, each a fast-forward. Neither pin was re-made: `facd8139` and `ba73674f` already name those shas. `../rosetta-pin` moved to `2a91bf0`.
- **Docs at source.**
  - `docs/agent-plane/api.html`: both doors, and `GET /api/activity` among rosettad's routes.
  - `docs/agent-plane/architecture.html` (`a87d73c5`): the history capability's row in the seams table; the monitor-ownership note names the capability; the MV row's stale "integration gates precede main landing" is corrected in its cell.
  - `docs/AGENT_PLANE.md`'s "runtime only" sentence and the 2026-10-03 laws in `docs/DECISIONS.md` each carry a dated note (this ledger's commit).
  - `DESIGN.md` §8, "Godview's timeline is the swarm through time" (this ledger's commit; the MV lead's words, every number read from puppeteer `c20a07d`). No commit of the chain had touched it, and five places still said the timeline kept no past. Each is corrected at its source: runtime only where no record is lent; the record's stretches, the dotted thread, the bounds band and the seam; an ended run's lane at 45%; the looking-back readouts; the map's worked stretches; "the timeline reads a record it does not keep". A TV pick that changes the look moves these lines with its commit.

**The view half (the MV lead's account, placed as written; puppeteer `vf/timeline-past-view` `c20a07d`):**

> **The timeline draws the record's past (the view half; MV lead, puppeteer `vf/timeline-past-view` `c20a07d`, 9 commits on `vf/monitor-history-port` `a4f088e`).** Docket v9 T0 (a) split the work: History built the read, and the view draws it.
>
> **What the view draws:**
> - **A live lane's past**, before its current state:
>   - work as the wake, in the project's colour;
>   - quiet as the hairline;
>   - a dotted thread wherever the record cannot say (an `unrecorded` span, or time no span covers);
>   - a 1 px seam in the ground colour where the record runs unbroken into the runtime's state.
> - **A run that ended** (TL-D6, restored from before MV-6 and fed by `history.ended`):
>   - faint, in its birth slot, with an end tick and no blur;
>   - named by the session's title;
>   - reading `last active 27m ago`;
>   - lit and readable, never opened: no command ever receives a `past:` id.
> - **The floor (T5):** one flat faint band per ended run; `–` · `detail not recorded`; never counted as work.
> - **The map of the day (T6):** counted from the same spans, plus the working rows since `statusSince`. Waits come only from model rows.
> - **The record's sentence** when it is partial or cannot be read: under SINCE; `RECORD PARTIAL` / `NO RECORD NOW` in the narrow head.
> - **With `history` absent:** exactly what it drew before. That covers puppeteer's own Godview, the phone, and a desktop with no record.

  its own 30 s (its body waits up to 15 s twice); doc-holders-stop's CONTROL row waits 10 s on a real ledger flush
  (the never-settling rows keep 100 ms); field-native's logging `flush(4 s)` test 15 s.

- `b14aaca3` doc-sync-service: a row waits on the commit it expects (`onCommit`), never a fixed 60 ms; afterEach stops
  the routing and disposes the store before the directory goes (`rmSync`'s retries stay as a backstop). Red first: the
  old wait tightened to 0 went ENOTEMPTY in 3 of 10 on the sightings' own two rows; fixed with the backstop REMOVED,
  0 of 10.
- `311b2034` terminal-kill-matrix row 6: a create refused UNAVAILABLE + retryable is asked again, 250 ms apart, for 30 s
  of the row's 60 s, each refusal printed, and the field-native log's tail printed before cleanup deletes it. Red first:
  the row forced to lose the birth race went red 5 of 5 with the sighting's words; fixed, 0 of 5. A dead floor still
  fails loudly at the budget.

`red-3-docsync-tightened.log`, `s3-docsync-fixed-no-backstop.log`, `red-4-killmatrix-birthrace.log`,
`probe-4-loud-failure.log`); then the landing gate on the exact tree (`lanes/land3/logs/`, under this landing's sha).

`flush(500 ms)` (:1431) can never write once two writes in a row have failed. Whether a requested flush cuts the

## Debts, fifth part — the four fieldd reds that met this day's landings were the tests' own races, each proven and fixed; one upstream finding for rosetta (2026-10-12; `d41fe1d8` · `4baff058` · `a8a6e35d` · `1e4bdbdb` through lane land3, gated on the exact tree)

**Why:** parts two to four each met fieldd reds on trees that did not touch fieldd (the fourth part's entry, "Found"
and "Owed"). Lane dfd diagnosed each; every fix is test-only, each proven red first by forcing the ordering it found
and green under the same probe (`/Volumes/SamsungRed/lanes/dfd/red-q*.log`, `q*-fixed-probe.log`). No product fault.

**What landed:**
- `d41fe1d8` agent-session (four sightings, the re-attach row): `auditAct` read the audit ledger once. The boot's
  background re-attach shows its row in agent.list and writes `reattach: attached` before its fsync'd outcome is
  appended (`AuditService.requiredAs` writes the attempt, runs the effect, then the outcome), and the row read the
  ledger in that gap. No outcome is ever dropped (later writes made 3 s late: 3/3 red before, 0/3 after). `auditAct`
  now waits up to 10 s; all 13 call sites await it.
- `4baff058` rosettad-supervisor (two sightings): the FAKE rosettad wrote its ready line before it installed its SIGINT
  handler, so a stop that came first killed it by Node's default and left its announce file behind; fieldd's supervisor
  did nothing wrong (stop() awaits the real exit; the red took 329 ms, no SIGKILL). The fake arms its guard first.

## TD-0 — the trust-root has a shape: `TrustRoot`, `UpdatePolicy` and `RegistryIndexV2` in contracts, `scripts/trust-keygen.mjs`, and the ledger's `trustRootKeys` waiting on James's keys (2026-10-14; ``11c8fa67``)

**Why:** the first rung of the trust ladder (`specs/trust-and-distribution.md` §9, ruled 2026-10-14, TD-1…TD-18), and
the second of the prod-builder brief's order of work. It gives every later rung its shapes and its one key tool: TD-1 (James
mints the root and the roles), TD-2 (WP8's bundled index under the `bundled` role), TD-3 (the signed update feed and
policy), TD-4 (the registry's index v2).

**What landed:**
- **contracts, `trust-root.ts`:** `TrustRoot` — TUF's fields and no other (TD-16): `schemaVersion`, a monotonic `version`,
  `expires`, the `root` key set and the three online roles. Keys are `Ed25519SpkiBase64`, the kit's encoding pinned to its
  60-character SPKI shape (a PKCS#8 secret can never pass). The threshold must be ≤ the keys. The root is at least two keys
  (TD-1), and EVERY key belongs to one role: the offline root is never an online key, and no role can sign another's
  documents. Also `judgeSignedDocument` (TD-10: `rollback` before anything else, `stale` past expiry, else `accepted`) and
  `TRUST_FRESHNESS_DAYS` (180 · 60 · 90).
- **contracts, `update-policy.ts`:** `UpdatePolicy` — EDP-37's levers (`yanked`, `killSwitch`, `requireUserConfirmation`,
  `floors`, `minSupported`) plus TD-3's `version`, `generatedAt`, `expires`, `channel` (nightly · beta · stable, RL4) and
  `trustRootVersion`. This is also WP12a's schema.
- **contracts, `plugin-distribution.ts`:** `RegistryIndexV2` beside v1 (§6.3). It carries publishers, rung, reviewer,
  capabilities, yanked, the kill switch with its reason, stats, and per release the source commit and the attestation
  digest. A plugin must sit in its publisher's namespace, its publisher must be registered, and it is keyed by its own id.
  `Sha256Pin` is exported.
- **Fixtures and refusals:** `trust-root.valid.json` (canonical, as `assemble` writes it), `update-policy.valid.json` and
  `registry-index-v2.valid.json` hold public keys only. `trust-root.test.ts` carries 21 refusals and judgements inline
  (every fixture file must parse). `tooling/plugin-build/test/trust-keygen-compat.test.ts` holds the script to the kit
  both ways: canonical JSON byte for byte, keypairs, and signatures made by one and verified by the other.
- **`scripts/trust-keygen.mjs`** (builtins only, so James runs it with no build): `keygen`, `assemble`, `sign`, `verify`,
  `embed`, `--self-test`. Its EL7 guards:
  - a secret is PRINTED once and only to a terminal; with stdout not a TTY it refuses unless `--secret-out` names a file,
    written 0600, never over a file and never inside the repository;
  - `sign` reads the secret from stdin (`security find-generic-password … -w | … --key-stdin`) or a named variable,
    never argv;
  - no key or document is overwritten.
  `trust-root.json.sig` holds one base64 signature per line, one line per root key (a one-line file is exactly the kit's
  registry signature). `verify` counts distinct trusted root keys against the threshold, refuses a rollback, and refuses
  an expired document in words. `embed` (TD-1) copies the verified document beside the packaging config, freezes
  `trustRootKeys` and bumps `identityRevision`. A second embedding is a rotation, verified against the first. The 23-row
  self-test runs in preflight.
- **The ledger and its checker:**
  - `release-identity.json` gains `trustRootKeys` as a TD-1 blocker (identityRevision 4 → 5).
  - `check-release-identity.mjs` gains a list format, `ed25519-spki-base64[]` (≥2 distinct keys), and a structural
    freeze compare.
  - The credential-blob rule now exempts a value only when it PROVES to be an Ed25519 public key, so a secret under that
    format is refused twice.
  - TD-1's consumer rule: the embedded `trust-root.json`'s root keys equal the frozen field, its `.sig` exists, and no
    embedded root exists while the field is a blocker.
  - `update-channel` accepts `nightly` (RL4).
  - 12 new self-test rows.
- **biome:** `**/trust-root.json` and the trust-root fixture are excluded. A signature covers exact bytes, and biome
  collapsing a one-key array would break every signature on the embedded copy.

## PJ-7, the first phone run's fixes — History says when the index is down and rebuilds it after an upgrade, a folder list never waits behind mille's watcher, the first launch sheet draws, an agent's card can attach again, and the index can be restarted from History (2026-10-14; `b030de84` · `347c8c89` · `e201c95a` · `c2860c5d` · `b99f8331` · `b0c00213` · `6da4cf2b` through lane land3, gated in full on the exact tree)

**Why:** James's computer-use tester ran PJ-7 on his iPhone (`draft/testing/pj7-phone-test-plan.md`; results
`draft/testing/pj7-phone-results-2026-10-14.md`): 6 PASS, 3 FAIL, 23 blocked. The block was environmental — the dev
History index sat at rosetta schema 24 under a rosettad that expects 27, and rosetta fails an old projection closed by
design; the lead ran `rosettad rebuild` on it (James: "just rebuild it") — but the run exposed what a user would meet
after any rosetta upgrade, and five more defects. James launched a session, **the fixer**, to "fix all the stuff"; it
built lane fix7 from the lead's brief (`draft/project-places/briefs/fix7.md`).

**What landed:**
- `b030de84` **fieldd rebuilds an index of another schema.** On rosetta's own mismatch line (`SchemaVersionMismatch {
  found, expected }`, or its Display form) the rosettad supervisor runs `rosettad rebuild` with the same `--db`,
  `--home` and `--enroll` serve gets — rosetta's validated rebuild into a private sibling, installed only when every
  runtime replays — says `rebuilding` (a new INDEX_PHASES value, golden `index-status.rebuilding`), then serves again.
  Once per mismatch; never charged to the restart intensity; a failed rebuild ends `failed` in rosetta's words. Before
  it, an upgraded user's History retried five times and stopped (the real-binary row on main's supervisor fails with the
  phone run's own words).
- `347c8c89` **the phone's History says its door's index** (a PJ-7 regression: the projects reader had dropped SP-6's
  `index.status`): starting, rebuilding, indexing · N %, or "studio's index has stopped" with fieldd's reason; "No
  project in your desktops' index yet" only over a ready index.
- `e201c95a` **a folder list never waits without end on its files engine.** The run's 20 s list timeouts were inside
  mille (`c8160d5`): every filesystem-facing call arms a recursive watcher on the engine's root, and its batches
  reconcile under the engine's one `policy_gate`, which `resync` needs too — one probe list on the SSD waited 44.5 s, 37 s
  of it in resync. On our side, without patching mille: a list waits at most 4 s on its engine and a held engine is
  retired for a fresh one, once; search resolves hits in a short-lived engine of its own, bounded and marked partial when
  cut; concurrent searches of one subtree share a walk. `engine.ts`'s "row-only engines have no watcher" is corrected at
  its source.
- `b99f8331` **the first launch sheet draws.** The blank sheet (`L8-blank-sheet.png`, full height, no title) was a
  presentation race: `.sheet(isPresented:)` read a model set in the same update; it is `.sheet(item:)` now. The sheet's
  rows also draw at once and say what they wait on, and the Agent row no longer says "No agent available" while reading.
- `b0c00213` **an agent's card attaches again.** fieldd was right — an adopted run's row carries its terminal — but the
  card had no act for it since TM-5 retired the store IOS-4c's ATTACH rode; only DEBUG `-vf-auto-attach` attached (as
  Phase 0 did). The card offers ATTACH for its own run's terminal.
  > **Correction (2026-10-15):** the phone's second run (on main `34a1171c`) showed the card's act restored but the
  > attach not working. ATTACH appeared and a tap minted its ticket, then nothing dialed, and the card read "connecting
  > over the mesh…" until the run had ended and after. An attach is not yet witnessed on a device. See the fix8 entry.
- `6da4cf2b` **Restart the index, in desktop History.** `system.index.restart` — the "restart affordance" fieldd's
  failed sentence named — had no caller, and could have none: it rode `native.admin`, which no window holds. It moves to
  `agents.manage` (the lead's ruling, recorded in the plan: the window holds it, local-only, never plugin-eligible; the
  index's enrolment already lives in Settings → Agents), and History's failed state carries the button; fieldd's
  sentence names it; the phone says the restart is in History on that desktop (no phone act, P2).
- `c2860c5d` **DEBTS:** agent-gateway's "row 3 — the shell exits under it" waits for the shell's death as it waits for the
  agent's (the MV lead's red on `562ea33a`; the floor's ladder ends the agent first, and a zombie reads alive); its four

## PJ-7, the second phone run's fixes — an attach never waits forever: it says where it stopped and on which desktop, a run that exits mid-attach is said as ended, and each step is written to the phone's console (2026-10-15; `3e515fe4` · `903d0773` through lane land3, gated in full on the exact tree)

**Why:** James's tester ran the PJ-7 plan a second time on his iPhone, on main `34a1171c` with fix7 in it
(`draft/testing/pj7-phone-results-2026-10-14-run2.md`): 4 PASS, 1 FAIL, 27 n/a.
- **Witnessed on the device:**
  - the dev index came up `ready`, with no schema mismatch;
  - three launch-sheet openings drew their rows at once (fix7's `b99f8331`);
  - Browse listed the SSD in 784 ms and the scratch folder in 772 ms, and a search inside the scratch folder answered
    in 475 ms (`e201c95a`);
  - the phone's Browse launch landed in the exact folder (audit `agent.session.spawn`, actor `tailnet`);
  - the agent's card offered ATTACH (`b0c00213`).
- **The FAIL (S2):** the tap minted one ticket (audit `terminal.ticket.mint` succeeded, 03:49:51Z). From then on the
  card read "connecting over the mesh…", still after the run had ended.
- **L8's missing project was the plan's error, not a defect:** History's places come only from rosetta's project rows
  (`place-scanner.ts`), and Claude writes no transcript before its first prompt, which the test agent never got. The
  launch's recipe waits meanwhile (`ProjectRecords.actedIn`). The plan is corrected at its source and now sends one
  prompt.

**What the lead found before the lane:**
- There was no second mint. The client re-mints on every lost leg, so no leg ever failed.
- The desktop's agent cell, which logs every leg that reaches its T1 door (refusals included), logged none.
- The desktop half works: from this Mac's own Tailscale node, a WebSocket upgrade to
  `:9422/cell/<the agent cell>/control` was answered 101 and then refused `PRE_AUTH_LIMIT`, so the terminal serve, the
  agent cell's route and the sidecar's WS forward (P0-H's T6) all hold.
- The stall is on the phone, between the ticket and the first socket.
- No phone has attached on hardware since P0-H (2026-09-25). The attach path has since gained SP-2's leg budget and
  DS-4b's seat (both 10-01). The phone's package pins have not moved since.

**What landed (the fixer, from the lead's brief `draft/project-places/briefs/fix8.md`):**
- `3e515fe4` **an attach never waits forever.**
  - `RoutedTerminalClient` derives the step it waits on from what it holds: ticket, slot, dial, control, frames or
    first frame. It re-derives the step after every leg event, slot grant and mint, and gives each step the same
    deadline, 20 s (the mesh's 15 s request timeout and a margin).
  - Past it, the set is torn down whole (legs, slots, a queued slot waiter, re-mints, renewals), and the state is
    `.stalled(step)`. The first mint races the same deadline, because the door's `call` waits for its hello first.
  - The card's banner: "couldn't reach studio's terminal", over the step in words ("the dial over the mesh got no answer —
    stopped after 20 s"), with RETRY (a fresh attach) and BACK TO THE FIELD. DESIGN.md §8 carries every sentence,
    written first.
  - A run whose face turns `exited` while the card is still attaching is said as ended ("its run exited on studio"),
    with RESUME, and stops dialing.
  - A live session is never stopped by these deadlines.
  - Also fixed: the slot task checks its own cancellation after `acquire` (a free ledger answers without suspending, so
    legs a refusal had torn down were opened anyway).
- `903d0773` **the attach says where it is on the device's console.**
  - `TerminalAttachLog.device` writes one line per phase to the unified log (`com.jamesyong.vibefield.kit` /
    `attach`, public arguments), and in DEBUG also prints it as `[attach] …`, which a `devicectl` stdout capture
    carries. Run 2's capture held only stdout.
  - Each leg's `node.urlSession(configuration:)` is bracketed with its elapsed ms.
  - `MainThreadWitness` (DEBUG only) logs "main thread stalled N s, last attach phase: …" when the main queue has not
    answered for 2 s, and its recovery.
  - A line carries only ids, refusal codes and error domains and numbers: never a grant, MAC, nonce or URL (a test).
  - `apps/ios/README.md` says how to read an attach on a device.

**Item 1, the cause, did not reproduce in the kit, and is not claimed.** Ruled out with tests:
- **the leg budget:** run 2's tap was the app's first attach; doors count against their own resource; and run 2's
  order of events attaches at once (`runTwosOrderAttachesAtOnce`);
- **a far end that takes the socket and never answers:** `URLSessionWebSocketTask` fails at its request timeout and
  the client re-mints (`aSilentDoorEndsInAFreshMint`), and run 2 had no second mint.

Two device-only readings remain: (a) the mesh's session factory never returned for a leg (TailscaleKit's `proxyVia` →
a synchronous `loopback()`); (b) the main thread stopped right after the mint (the tester's `···` tap and swipe drew
nothing, and the card's header still said `idle` sixteen seconds after the run exited). Run 3's console decides:
- a last line "asking the mesh for a session", with no "mesh session in", is (a);
- "main thread stalled" is (b), with the phase it stopped in.

## WP8 — the packaged app carries its own plugins under a signed index: the browser, the browser pane and the pad staged under the trust-root's `bundled` role, verified by fieldd at two grains, and a package with no identity refused (2026-10-15; `40178d20` `5e7507d6`)

**Why:** ESP §10.4 / §16 item 4. Until now every packaged build shipped ZERO built-ins: the stager's `plugins/bundled`
row was null, electron-builder dropped the empty folder, and `package:mac:release` could not pass, because
`--require-complete` turned that absent row into a failure. WP8 is the third rung of the prod-builder brief's order of
work and TD-2 of the trust ladder: the bundled index is signed by the `bundled` role of the trust-root TD-0 shaped.
Plan: `draft/specs/build-wp8-bundled-plugins.md` (with its §10 addendum).

**What landed:**
- **WP8a, the shape and the kit's verifier.**
  - contracts: `BundledPluginIndex` / `BundledPluginEntry` / `StagedPluginPath` / `BundledPluginPlatform`. Each entry
    carries every staged file's hash, the manifest hash (fieldd's own definition) and the artifact hash (`packVfplugin`
    over the staged tree, the registry's pin for the same bytes).
  - The names are in registries.ts: the index, its `.sig` (the kit's convention, which amends ESP §10.1's
    `bundled-plugins.sig`), `identity/`, `release-identity.json`, `FIELDD_TRUST_ROOT(_KEYS)`. They are TS-only.
  - The kit has `buildBundledIndex` / `verifyBundledIndex` and `trust.ts`. W2's six refusals each name their file.
- **WP8b, the stage produces it.**
  - `bundled-plugins.mjs` (stage/verify). DEV mints an ephemeral trust-root in memory and drops its secrets. RELEASE
    needs `VIBEFIELD_BUNDLED_INDEX_SECRET` and the embedded trust-root, and refuses while `trustRootKeys` is a TD-1
    blocker.
  - `bundled-list.mjs` holds the one named list.
  - The stager's null row is gone: its producer's verdict is required, `identity/` is a stage root, and
    `--require-release-key` exists. The report line reads `plugins/bundled: … KEY CLASS: DEV|RELEASE`.
  - electron-builder ships `identity/`, and `StagedReleaseIdentity` is in contracts.
- **WP8c, fieldd verifies; the shell hands over and refuses.**
  - fieldd: a keyed bundled root checks the trust-root against the app's root keys at its own threshold, then the index
    against the `bundled` role, then each plugin's bytes. A bad trust-root or index is one root problem and no row. A
    bad copy is that row `invalid` with `PLUGIN_ARTIFACT_MISMATCH`, naming the path. A verified row's installRevision
    is its artifact hash, and it carries a provenance block.
  - shell: `DesktopResources.identity` and `readBundledTrust`, plus three typed packaged-only refusals:
    `bundled-identity-missing`, `bundled-root-missing`, and `bundled-dev-trust` (a DEV stage launches only with
    `--allow-dev-trust`).
  - WP8-D9: a packaged fieldd's roots and trust anchor come from the layout alone, never from the environment.
- **WP8d, the witnesses.** `pnpm smoke:bundled` is gate:landing's row 29 (three launches: loads · corrupt · forged).
  `package:verify:plugins --app <VibeField.app>` checks the BUILT app offline and then runs its packaged fieldd SEA.
  run-macos-release passes `--require-release-key` and runs the plugins verifier after the history verifier.

**Validation:**

- W6: `package:verify` ok. `--require-release-key` refuses the dev stage: `BUNDLED  KEY CLASS: DEV — a release stage must be signed with the release keys (set VIBEFIELD_BUNDLED_INDEX_SECRET; TD-1)`, exit 1.
